subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should OpenClaw establish `resetSession(reason?)` as an after-compaction-only plugin contract, or expose it across generic embedded-agent hook contexts?
rationale: This adds a permanent plugin-facing session lifecycle capability, and implementation details cannot safely determine which hook families should be authorized to request a reset or what availability guarantees external plugins may rely on.

options.title: Approve after-compaction only
options.body: Expose the method only on all after-compaction contexts and flush through a shared lifecycle owner after every compaction implementation has fully exited.

options.title: Approve a generic hook API
options.body: Expose it across embedded hook contexts only after documenting availability, authorization, deduplication, and lifecycle semantics for every affected hook family.

options.title: Decline the core capability
options.body: Keep session reset outside hook contexts and require plugins to use a separately approved extension or user-command workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve after-compaction only
recommendation.body: Expose the method only on all after-compaction contexts and flush through a shared lifecycle owner after every compaction implementation has fully exited.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the affected context-engine lifecycle and have adjacent ownership history in the gateway reset implementation.
